OpenAI Scales Back Funding Goal to $20 B, Sources Say

31 Oct 2026, 10:13 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: techcrunch.com

3 min read

Key takeaways---

Summary

OpenAI is reportedly lowering the size of its upcoming private funding round from an earlier target of $30 billion to $20 billion, according to the Financial Times (FT) and the Wall Street Journal (WSJ). The shift comes after the company secured roughly $11 billion to date and faced a “tepid” response from some large investors. The round will be led by investors from the United Arab Emirates, with a potential retail tranche for high‑net‑worth individuals that could bring total commitments up to the revised target.

---

Background

  • Original expectations: Earlier reports indicated OpenAI was seeking $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, later adjusted to a $1.25 trillion valuation ahead of a planned IPO.
  • Current revision: The FT article dated 31 Oct 2026 states the company has lowered its funding target to $20 billion and anticipates a first close that will be “even lower” than that figure.
  • Secured capital: The WSJ notes that OpenAI has already secured $11 billion in commitments.

---

New Funding Target Details

  • Lead investors: A consortium of investors based in the United Arab Emirates will head the round, according to the FT.
  • Retail component: The FT mentions a subsequent offering aimed at wealthy individuals, which could help reach the $20 billion goal.
  • Timeline: No specific dates for the first close or final close have been disclosed in the sources.

---

Investor Response

  • Tepid interest: The WSJ describes the reaction from some large investors as “tepid,” suggesting a more cautious appetite for large‑scale AI infrastructure funding.
  • Market sentiment: TechCrunch’s reporting links the softer response to broader Wall Street wariness of heavy AI‑related capital expenditures, which has contributed to a recent sell‑off in tech stocks.

---

Market Context

  • AI spending slowdown: Recent market data show a slowdown in venture capital allocations to AI infrastructure, as investors reassess risk amid high‑cost compute demands.
  • Competing IPOs: Anthropic, another AI startup, is reportedly facing challenges with its own IPO plans, adding to the perception of a tougher fundraising environment for AI firms.

---

Practical Implications

  • For OpenAI: A reduced funding ceiling may temper the pace of new product development or large‑scale compute investments, though the company still retains a substantial war chest.
  • For investors: The involvement of UAE investors signals continued international interest in AI, while the retail tranche could open opportunities for accredited investors seeking exposure.
  • For the AI ecosystem: A more modest capital influx could slow the rapid expansion of AI services, potentially affecting downstream developers and enterprises that rely on OpenAI’s models.

---

How to Verify the Announcement

  1. Check the original FT story – Look for the article published on 31 Oct 2026 that details the revised target and lead investors.
  2. Review the WSJ report – Confirm the $11 billion figure and the description of investor sentiment.
  3. Monitor OpenAI’s official channels – Press releases, blog posts, or SEC filings (if the company files a Form D for the private placement) will provide definitive numbers.
  4. Watch for follow‑up coverage – Reputable outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg, or The Information may publish additional details once the round progresses.

---

What Remains Unknown

  • Exact size of the first close – Both the FT and WSJ only indicate it will be “lower” than $20 billion, without a precise amount.
  • Final valuation – While earlier reports cited $1.25 trillion, the current valuation tied to the $20 billion target has not been disclosed.
  • Timeline for the IPO – No updated schedule has been provided.

---

*The article is based on reporting from the Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal as referenced by TechCrunch on 31 Oct 2026. No direct statements from OpenAI were obtained at the time of writing.*
